subdomain: 4.4 Diagnose system issues (prompt failure, hallucinations, model mismatch)

en.question: On multi-step allocation tasks, generated plans violate constraints despite verified evidence, correct tool fixtures, and a validated constraint checker. Output limits are not reached. Unclear instructions and a model capability mismatch remain plausible. Which controlled comparisons help distinguish these explanations? Select 2 answers.

options.text: Keep the model and fixtures fixed while testing a clearer constraint-focused prompt.
options.note: A prompt-only comparison tests whether clearer instructions resolve the failures without changing model capability or evidence. The same cases and checker make its outcome interpretable.

options.text: Replace the model, planner prompt, retrieval pipeline, and checker in one experiment.
options.note: Changing every component can yield a better system but cannot attribute the improvement to instructions or model capability. Replacing the validated checker also changes the meaning of success.

options.text: Raise the output limit and compare only each model's best-looking completed plan.
options.note: The limit is not implicated, and selecting best-looking outputs changes the comparison criterion. This does not isolate either instruction clarity or constraint-solving reliability.

options.text: Compare candidate models on the same clear prompt, fixtures, cases, and constraint checker.
options.note: Holding those factors fixed tests whether model choice changes constraint satisfaction under the same well-specified task. It provides evidence for or against a capability mismatch rather than assuming a stronger model is the remedy.

references.title: Anthropic Engineering: Demystifying evals for AI agents
